commits.message:
A tween eases a value from one to another over seconds (rich-animation-42lg.bjh)

`tween(from, to, timing)` in `src/core/tween.ts`: `from` before 0, eased
toward `to` through `Phase.once(0, seconds)`, held at `to` from then on,
with `nextChange` saying so — until 0, every frame, never. The blend is
`(1 − p)·from + p·to`, exact at both ends where `from + (to − from)·p` is
not, so a count lands on its target whatever the ease.

`Timing` is the ease-and-seconds pair, in `easing.ts`: what `spring()`
returns (replacing the `Spring` interface, the same shape under the name
of its one producer) and what an effect's `Curve` now extends, so a spring
is handed to a tween as it is.

A colour tween is `ColorRamp.over(seconds)`: the ramp's span crossed at a
steady rate, each colour the ramp's own, so the blending stays in one
place. Retargeting is `Animation.sequence(old, t₁, tween(old.at(t₁), to,
timing))`, documented and tested, with no state kept.

`docs/animation.md` gains the tween section; the colour studio demo gains
a tween row, which is what demonstrates the export to the coverage gate.

A timeline maps host time to animation time: pause, reverse, scrub, speed (rich-animation-42lg.kjt) (#479)

* A timeline maps host time to animation time: pause, reverse, scrub, speed (rich-animation-42lg.kjt)

A `Timeline` in `src/core/` is the map from the host's clock to the time an
animation is asked for, as a value: play, pause, resume, seek, a rate —
negative to reverse — each a timeline in and a timeline out, with no clock
read. `Timeline.run` is an animation on host time whose `nextChange` is
carried back onto the host's clock, the argument `Spinner`'s speed scaled
its holds for, now made once above the type; `Spinner`'s speed is a timeline.

Reversing exactly needs the other end of a hold, so `Animation` answers
`lastChange(t)` beside `nextChange(t)`: the last moment the value may have
become `at(t)`, which `Beat.start` already was and is now named for. Every
combinator and instance answers it. The spinner's drawn cells are restamped
with the host's answer (`Style.withNextChange`), since the frame's own
stamp is on the spinner's timeline.

effects-feel's hand-rolled `Pace` is a timeline over the frame count, and
space now pauses it.

* A timeline's host moment is a search across clocks, and a frame is stamped where it is drawn (rich-animation-42lg.kjt)

Review findings, high pass. Timeline.run threw for any animation time far from
the host's or any slow rate, backwards above all: a host float is a step of
`rate` on the animation's clock, so the floats between the sum and the first
one past an edge are as many as the two clocks' resolutions are apart, which
the eight-ulp walk for a sum on one clock cannot cover. `firstReaching` in
easing.ts brackets and halves to the exact float; `played` is one shape for
both directions, with the host time refused once at entry.

FrameSequence.at stamped its cells with nextChange on its own clock, so a
sequence run on a timeline, or after an Animation.sequence switch, handed a
host a stamp it could not read; Spinner was re-stamping over it, overwriting
a label's earlier word. `at` is now the frame alone and `frameAt` stamps it
where a host time is known — Frames, Spinner, the template `frames` function
— so Style.withNextChange and the re-stamping loop go. Spinner's copy of the
rate check goes too; the timeline is the one enforcer. A paused timeline
refuses a non-finite host time at seek like every other operation.

* frameAt is public and stamps a copy, and an edge past the host's clock is never (rich-animation-42lg.kjt)

Review findings, medium pass. `frameAt` is exported from the main barrel
and the showcase blinks a cursor through it, since a line assembled from
`sequence.at(t)` lost its stamp when the stamp moved off `at`. It stamps a
copy: an animation may hand back the one text it holds, as
`Animation.constant` does, and a stamp on that outlived its draw. A sum
that overflows the host's clock — a subnormal rate, an edge 1e308 host
seconds off — is the never it signs, not a bracket of NaN that never closes;
`firstReaching` refuses an infinite guess outright.

* firstReaching stays within the finite floats, and a sequence's carried moment is searched both ways (rich-animation-42lg.kjt)

Review findings, escalation high. The downward bracket could step onto
-Infinity and bisect NaN forever; the search now clamps to the finite floats
and answers always or never at either end. Animation.sequence carried a
moment by walking up from a sum that can round over the change as well as
under it, so nextChange was a float late on about one time in forty; it is
the same search now, and the test asserts the float before the answer still
shows the old value. A paused run refuses a non-finite host time like a
playing one. A stray file `1` left at the root by the last commit is gone.
